# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36 (Bi-Vb Pc36)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 36. Socializing with a householder
**Title (English, from literature):** Socializing with a householder

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁsaṭṭha Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 36) is a rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka prohibiting a Buddhist nun from living in ongoing or inappropriate socialization with a householder or a householder's son (*saṁsaṭṭhā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā*) [Hüsken 1997; Wijayaratna 1990; Collett 2014; SuttaCentral]. According to the origin story, the rule was promulgated when the nun Caṇḍakālī maintained an overly intimate relationship with a lay householder and his son [Collett 2014]. If a nun persistently engages in such inappropriate association despite being reproved, she must confess a *pācittiya* offense [SuttaCentral].

Scholars have drawn attention to the unusual formal procedure encoded in this rule: Ute Hüsken observes that Pācittiya 36 is the only rule for nuns outside the *saṅghādisesa* class that prescribes a formal threefold admonition (*samanubhāsanā*), a procedural requirement otherwise alien to the *pācittiya* category [Hüsken 1997]. This unique structure is corroborated by DharmaNexus text-reuse computations, which show that its longest matching blocks are shared precisely with admonition formulas in *saṅghādisesa* rules, including Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 10, 11, 12, and 13, as well as several Bhikkhu *saṅghādisesa* counterparts [DharmaNexus].

Full parallels to the rule are attested across all major extant Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels listed on SuttaCentral include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pc* 36) and Parivāra, the Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda Sanskrit Vibhaṅga (*pc* 86), and the Chinese Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Dharmaguptaka (*pc* 99), Mahīśāsaka (*pc* 210), Sarvāstivāda (*pc* 163), and Mahāsaṅghika (*pc* 86) traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently identifies textual alignments with the Tibetan Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga (D0005) and Vinayavastu (D0001), as well as the Sanskrit *Pāṇḍulohitakavastu* [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
